name: level-ground-then-build
description: #1009: ordering `level_ground` over a rectangle of uneven ground queues excavation work for a qualified rock_digger driver instead of carving anything synchronously. For seed:42's default staffed map, the 2x2 rect (14,17)-(15,18) sits on a genuine one-voxel step (surface Y=36 at x:14, Y=35 at x:15, across both z rows) — exactly management_office tier1's own 2x2 footprint. `build management_office at:14,17` is refused first (baseline: #1008's flat-footprint rule is live), then `level_ground minX:14 maxX:15 minZ:17 maxZ:18` is ordered and ticked to completion, after which the identical build order succeeds. `level_ground`/`build` steps are deliberately left untagged (no role) rather than 'player': BuildMenu.ts's ground-levelling section (`makeLevelGroundSection`) is still a skeleton stub with no real drag-a-rectangle control wired yet, so no click sequence exists to replay here — the visual-tester phase converts these to real `dragTiles` interactions once that UI lands.

steps.description: Staffed opening (#551): 5 employees (including two driving.excavator-qualified drivers) and 4 vehicles (including one rock_digger), matching STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION (balance.ts) — the same roster building-ramp-visual.json relies on for its own rock_digger work.

Staffed vehicles come unmanned (#551) — crew rock_digger #3 with driver #4, one of the two driving.excavator-qualified drivers STARTING_SITE_STAFFED_COMPOSITION grants, before ordering any excavation work. Mirrors building-ramp-visual.json's identical bootstrap step.
Baseline: the rect is genuinely uneven (Y=36 at x:14, Y=35 at x:15) so #1008's flat-footprint rule refuses the order outright, before any level_ground order exists to make this pass.

expect.note: Refused synchronously — no PlannedBuilding was queued for the uneven footprint.

steps.description: Order ground-levelling over the same uneven rect. No BuildMenu control exists for this yet (see the scenario-level description), so this step stays untagged rather than 'player' until that UI lands.

expect.note: Order-time cost (2 excess voxels x LEVEL_GROUND_COST_PER_VOXEL) is charged immediately, mirroring build_ramp's own order-then-work pattern.

steps.description: Drain the queued level_ground work — a qualified rock_digger driver walks to the rect and carves the 2 excess voxels down to the lower bench. Generously padded: the job itself is tiny (2 voxels), so this bounds travel time, not excavation time.
The identical build order that was refused before levelling now succeeds — the rect reads as flat once the level_ground action has landed.

expect.note: Accepted and queued for construction — proves the flattened area now passes #1008's flat-footprint rule.
